title: Unsafe `shell=True` grep interpolates snapshot filenames in `scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py`
body:
**Description**

`scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py` builds a `grep` command by interpolating snapshot
filenames from the working tree into a shell string that is then executed with
`shell=True`, so shell metacharacters in committed snapshot filenames execute
arbitrary commands when the script is run.

In `scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py` (lines 225-228):

```python
cmd = f'grep -r --include="*.py" "{snapshot_name}" e2e_playwright/'
result = subprocess.run(
    cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False
)
```

The `snapshot_name` is derived from on-disk filenames (lines 288-311):

```python
for dirpath, _, filenames in os.walk(snapshot_root):  # e2e_playwright/__snapshots__/linux
    for filename in filenames:
        if filename.endswith(".png"):
            all_snapshot_files.append(os.path.join(dirpath, filename))
...
snapshot_name = re.sub(r"\[.*\]\.png$", "", filename)
```

`filename` comes straight from the repository working tree (the snapshot PNGs
are committed to git), so anyone whose snapshot file gets merged controls part
of the command string. Because the value is placed inside double quotes,
`/bin/sh` still interprets `"`, `;`, `|`, `$()` and backticks — for example a
file named `st_button"; touch /tmp/pwned; "[chromium].png` is reduced to the
snapshot name `st_button"; touch /tmp/pwned; "` and produces

    grep -r --include="*.py" "st_button"; touch /tmp/pwned; "" e2e_playwright/

which runs `touch /tmp/pwned` as a separate command. The remaining grep then
searches for the same injected string, keeping the script's normal flow intact.

**Trigger scenario**

1. A PR adds (or renames) a snapshot file under
   `e2e_playwright/__snapshots__/linux/` with a filename containing shell
   metacharacters (the name is visible in the diff, but its effect is easy to
   miss in review).
2. The PR is merged.
3. A maintainer runs `python scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py` locally, or CI runs
   it in `--ci` mode — both paths execute the grep above.
4. The injected command executes in the maintainer's environment / CI runner.

**Impact**

Arbitrary command execution in the environment of whoever runs the cleanup
script. In practice the attacker already needs write access to the repository
(a merged PR), so I'd class this as a hardening issue rather than a security
vulnerability — which is why I'm opening a regular issue instead of using a
security channel. Still, it's an easy footgun to eliminate: the `find` call a
few lines above (lines 157-160) also uses `shell=True` (its string is static,
so it is harmless, but it could be cleaned up in the same pass).

**Suggested fix**

Drop the shell entirely and pass an argument list, keeping `--` to avoid
option injection:

```python
result = subprocess.run(
    ["grep", "-r", "--include=*.py", "--", snapshot_name, "e2e_playwright/"],
    capture_output=True, text=True, check=False,
)
```

Optionally validate the name as defense in depth, e.g.
`re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]+", snapshot_name)` (or use `shlex.quote()` if a
shell must be kept).

I'd be happy to open a PR switching both `shell=True` call sites to the
argument-list form if that's welcome. Thanks for maintaining a great project!

comments.body:
`scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py` interpolates snapshot PNG basenames into a `grep` command string and runs it with `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)`. The names come from `os.walk` of `e2e_playwright/__snapshots__/linux/` after only stripping a `[browser].png` suffix, so shell metacharacters in a snapshot filename can break out of the double quotes and run extra commands. This is confirmed in `search_for_snapshot_name` (around lines 225–228). The nearby `find` call also uses `shell=True`, but its command string is static. Impact is limited to whoever runs the script: maintainers locally, and CI via `.github/workflows/snapshot-hygiene.yml` (including on PRs that change `e2e_playwright/**`, so a merge is not required for CI execution). This is maintainer/CI hardening rather than a user-facing Streamlit vulnerability. Passing an argv list (with `--`) instead of a shell string is the correct fix.

### Related Issues

- [#16691](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16691) — Defense-in-depth against interpolating filenames into a protocol field. Same class of unescaped-filename issue, different surface (`st.file_uploader`, not this script).
- [#16631](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16631) — Interpolating a filename containing quotes into a `Content-Disposition` header without escaping. Related interpolation bug, not a duplicate.

No existing issues track `snapshot_cleanup.py` or this `shell=True` grep path.

---
*This is an automated triage comment using `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*

Thanks for the triage. One point worth stating explicitly, since it raises the stakes beyond "whoever runs the script": because `.github/workflows/snapshot-hygiene.yml` runs on PRs touching `e2e_playwright/**`, an attacker does **not** need a merge — opening a PR that adds a snapshot file with shell metacharacters in its name is enough for the injected command to execute in the CI runner on that PR's checkout.

Repro from the original report, for whoever picks up the fix:

```bash
cd <repo-root>
mkdir -p e2e_playwright/__snapshots__/linux
touch 'e2e_playwright/__snapshots__/linux/st_button"; touch /tmp/pwned; "[chromium].png'
python scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py --dry-run   # same grep path as --ci
ls /tmp/pwned   # exists => injection executed
```

Agreed on the fix — argv list with `--` — and the static `find` call a few lines above can be converted in the same pass. Still happy to open the PR if that's welcome.

> an attacker does not need a merge — opening a PR that adds a snapshot file with shell metacharacters in its name is enough for the injected command to execute in the CI runner on that PR's checkout.

[USER] we have made the decision to not accept PRs from external contributors currently because we found we did not have the capacity to support reviewing these PRs -- the volume of PRs had greatly increased with the advance in agent technology. Thank you for engaging with the project by opening this issue -- opening bug reports and feature requests is how users can best contribute to the project!

CI does not run on external PRs from contributors that are not on our maintainer team, when PRs submissions were open, a maintainer always approved the CI to run after reviewing the contents for security. 

I will take a look at how we might harden this while not impacting our current workflows, thank you for submitting this issue!
